s uper Scrabble Brand Crossword Game® inventor, Murray L.
Eskenazi, Lambda '56 says he came up with the game 33 years
ago while playing Scrabble® solitaire. Near the end of the game
-
he had a seven letter word that he could not play because there was no room
on the board . His annoyance with the board being too small turned into a
brilliant variation, which he originally called Double Scrabble. The game
strategy is slightly different but you have to play the game to appreciate the
subtle nature of the differences.
In 1995 he sent the game to Milton Bradley, w ho was then producing
Scrabble and they rejected it . In 2002 , when he was planning on retirement
he renamed it " Master Scrabble " but offered " Super Scrabble as an
alternative. A friend in Chicago located a game agent who knew the president
of Hasbro ( Hasbro owns the U.S. and Canadian rights to Scrabble ® ) and sent
him the game. The president of Hasbro sent the game to the National
Scrabble Association for comment . They sent back a favorable review and
Hasbro decided to market the game through Winning Moves Games, one of
its affiliated companies. They liked the name Super Scrabble and decided to
use that .

was able to do in three months what I couldn' t do on my own in 30 years."
He offers this advice to other inventors, " If your invention is not in the field in
which you are currently doing business, get an agent or someone w ho knows
-
the other industry to be your rep and give the agent a piece of the action . "
